- If sentiment shows strong negative or positive bias (e.g., -1.00 or 1.00) in recent days, reduce forecast slope or adjust mean to align with sentiment direction.  
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >5% from prior day), model tends to overcorrect — cap forecast rise to 3–5% max for next 3–5 days.  
- When sentiment is neutral or mixed (0.00–0.25), model often overestimates mean — apply downward bias of 1–2% to forecast mean.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 70), model tends to lag — adjust forecast to match recent low trend.  
- For 30-day horizon, if model consistently overpredicts by >2% over 3–5 days, reduce forecast slope by 0.5–1.0% per day.  
- If sentiment history includes multiple -1.00 or 1.00 entries, model may be overconfident — reduce forecast volatility by 10–20% for next 5 days.
